commit.message:
feat(mdk-core): accept caller-supplied d-tag for KeyPackage events (#303)

* feat(mdk-core): accept caller-supplied d-tag for KeyPackage events

Adds a `KeyPackageOptions::existing_d_tag: Option<String>` field so callers
rotating a KeyPackage can pass back the previously stored `d` tag instead of
post-editing the `Tag::identifier(...)` in `tags_30443` after the fact. When
`Some(d)`, the value is validated (non-empty, <= 128 chars, ASCII hex digits)
and threaded into both the kind:30443 `d` tag and the returned
`KeyPackageEventData::d_tag` — no random generation, no MLS impact (the
d-tag is purely a NIP-33 envelope concern).

`create_key_package_for_event_with_options` now takes `KeyPackageOptions`
in place of the bare `protected: bool`. The matching UniFFI binding mirrors
the struct as a `uniffi::Record`. `create_key_package_for_event` (the
no-options variant) is unchanged.

Closes the ergonomics gap noted in marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#835.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: rustfmt the no-options call-site

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` on the previous commit flagged the single-line
forward in `create_key_package_for_event` as exceeding the line-width limit.
Apply the canonical rustfmt-suggested break across multiple lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: address coderabbitai feedback on KeyPackageOptions

- Tighten `validate_existing_d_tag` to require exactly 64 ASCII hex digits
  (per MIP-00), matching the constraint enforced by `parse_key_package`. The
  previous 128-char cap created a round-trip footgun where a caller could
  supply a long `existing_d_tag` that passed creation validation but would
  later be rejected by `parse_key_package`. Renamed the constant to
  `D_TAG_HEX_LEN = 64` and updated the `wrong_length` test to cover both
  too-short and too-long inputs.
- Make `validate_existing_d_tag` public so consumers (and the UniFFI binding)
  can pre-validate using the canonical core helper.
- UniFFI `KeyPackageOptions`: replace the infallible `From` conversion with a
  `TryFrom` that runs `validate_existing_d_tag` at the FFI boundary and maps
  validation failures to `MdkUniffiError::InvalidInput`. Mirrors the pattern
  used by `parse_public_key` / `parse_relay_urls`, so a malformed parameter
  surfaces as a parameter error rather than a generic `Mdk` failure.
- Append `([#303](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/mdk/pull/303))` trailer
  to both new Unreleased CHANGELOG entries to match the crate's link format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: drop private intra-doc link from validate_existing_d_tag rustdoc

CI's Documentation jobs run with `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, which promotes
`rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links` to a hard error. The previous commit made
`validate_existing_d_tag` public but its rustdoc still referenced the private
`D_TAG_HEX_LEN` constant via `[`D_TAG_HEX_LEN`]`. Replace the intra-doc link
with plain prose ("exactly 64 hex characters (32 random bytes, hex-encoded —
per MIP-00)"). Keeps the constant private (smaller public API surface) while
the doc still communicates the rule.

Verified locally with `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps -p
mdk-core -p mdk-uniffi`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(encrypted_media): use deterministic timestamp for legacy-media compat tests

`test_decrypt_from_download_current_epoch_legacy_media_compat` and
`test_decrypt_from_download_epoch_hint_legacy_media_compat` called the
real-time `decrypt_from_download`, which fails once the MIP-03/MIP-04 legacy
exporter-secret migration deadline expires (2026-05-15 00:00:00 UTC per the
Unreleased CHANGELOG entry for #222). Both tests are now failing on every PR
against master starting today.

The deterministic `decrypt_from_download_at` variant was introduced by #222
precisely for this — switch the two tests to call it with
`fixed_pre_deadline_ts()`, mirroring the pattern already used by
`test_decrypt_from_download_current_epoch_legacy_disabled_after_deadline`
and friends elsewhere in the same module.

Not strictly related to the KeyPackage d-tag work in this PR, but bundling
the fix here unblocks CI for #303 (and every other PR currently failing on
the same calendar bomb).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: factor d-tag validation into shared validate_d_tag_value helper

Both `validate_existing_d_tag` (creation path) and `MDK::parse_key_package`
(parse path) enforced the same MIP-00 d-tag rules (non-empty, exactly 64 chars,
ASCII hex digits) — but in two textually separate places. The previous commit
made the behavioral symmetry argument in a docstring, but coderabbitai
correctly pointed out that "same rule, two implementations" is drift-prone.

Extract `validate_d_tag_value(d, field_name)` as the single source of truth.
`validate_existing_d_tag` becomes a one-line wrapper. `parse_key_package`
swaps its three inline checks (empty / length / hex::decode) for a single
call. The `field_name` parameter keeps error messages context-appropriate
("existing_d_tag must…" vs "d tag must…").

The "Missing required d tag" branch in `parse_key_package` stays as-is —
that's tag-presence (structural), not value validation (semantic), so it
doesn't belong in the shared helper.

No test asserts on the changed parse-side error message text (verified by
grep across all crates) — all parse-side tests use loose
`matches!(_, Err(Error::KeyPackage(_)))` assertions, which continue to pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: document UniFFI breaking change + add binding-level d-tag tests

Reviewer noted that `crates/mdk-uniffi/CHANGELOG.md` had no Unreleased entry
for the binding signature change — consumers reading only the UniFFI
changelog would miss that their call sites must change. Add a Breaking
changes entry covering the `protected: bool` → `KeyPackageOptions`
signature change and the new `MdkUniffiError.InvalidInput` mapping for
malformed `existing_d_tag`. Add an Added entry for the new
`KeyPackageOptions` record. Both reference PR #303 in the standard format.

Also fold in three direct binding-level behavioral tests, since the new
conversion path previously had only compile + binding-check coverage:

- `test_create_key_package_with_options_existing_d_tag`: a valid reused
  `existing_d_tag` appears in `KeyPackageResult.d_tag` and as the value of
  the `d` tag in `tags`.
- `test_create_key_package_with_options_invalid_d_tag`: malformed
  `existing_d_tag` surfaces as `MdkUniffiError::InvalidInput` at the FFI
  boundary, not as a generic `Mdk` error.
- `test_create_key_package_with_options_protected_tag`: `protected: true`
  still emits the NIP-70 `["-"]` tag — the new options struct preserves
  the previous bool's behavior.

All three pass; the uniffi test suite is now 77/77.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: expose KeyPackageOptions field defaults through UniFFI

coderabbitai correctly noted that `#[derive(uniffi::Record, Default)]` does
NOT translate Rust's `Default` impl into bindings-level defaults — foreign
callers in Swift / Kotlin / Python must explicitly construct each field
unless the field carries a `#[uniffi(default = ...)]` attribute. The doc
on `KeyPackageOptions` was therefore misleading: it promised "default
values" but bindings consumers couldn't actually omit fields.

Annotate both fields with their literal FFI defaults (`protected = false`,
`existing_d_tag = None`) so the generated Kotlin / Swift / Python bindings
expose them as optional constructor parameters. The Rust-side `Default`
derive stays — it's orthogonal to the FFI annotation and lets Rust callers
write `KeyPackageOptions::default()` (currently unused but harmless).

Update the rustdoc to reflect the actual FFI ergonomics: foreign callers
can now omit either or both fields, e.g. Kotlin
`KeyPackageOptions()` is equivalent to
`KeyPackageOptions(protected = false, existingDTag = null)`. The
"Check Bindings" CI job will regenerate the foreign bindings to pick up
the new defaults.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
